'''Alan David White''' (1923 — 9 May 2020) was an American physicist, known primarily as one of the inventors of the visible [[helium-neon laser]].

== Biography ==
After completing his military service during World War II, White graduated due to the [[G.I. Bill]]. He earned degrees in physics and mathematics from [[Rutgers University]] and [[Syracuse University]]. From 1953 to 1983 he worked at [[Bell Laboratories]]. Then he was a scientific consultant for Tropel Corp.

He was fond of art, in particular, sculpture.

For his achievements he was awarded the 1984 [[IEEE David Sarnoff Award]], and in 2000 he was elected to the [[New Jersey Inventors Hall of Fame]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2000 Awardees |url=http://www.njinvent.org/2000-awardees.html |access-date=2022-10-28 |website=NJ Inventors Hall of Fame 2018 |language=en}}</ref>

== Scientific achievements ==
The first gas laser, using a mixture of helium and neon, was demonstrated in 1960 and emitted radiation at a wavelength of 1.15 μm (infrared range).<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Javan |first1=A. |last2=Bennett |first2=W. R. |last3=Herriott |first3=D. R. |date=1961-02-01 |title=Population Inversion and Continuous Optical Maser Oscillation in a Gas Discharge Containing a He-Ne Mixture |journal=Physical Review Letters |volume=6 |issue=3 |pages=106–110 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.6.106|bibcode=1961PhRvL...6..106J |doi-access=free }}</ref> Two years later, White, together with Dane Rigden, showed that a [[Helium–neon laser|helium-neon laser]] can emit radiation at a wavelength of 632.8 nm, i.e., in the visible range of the spectrum.<ref>{{Cite journal |date=July 1962 |title=Correspondence |journal=Proceedings of the IRE |volume=50 |issue=7 |pages=1683–1713 |doi=10.1109/JRPROC.1962.288157 |issn=2162-6634}}</ref> In subsequent years, White, with [[Eugene I. Gordon]] and others, investigated the reasons for the limitation of the power of such lasers,<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Gordon |first1=E. I. |last2=White |first2=A. D. |date=1963-12-01 |title=SIMILARITY LAWS FOR THE EFFECTS OF PRESSURE AND DISCHARGE DIAMETER ON GAIN OF He–Ne LASERS |url=https://aip.scitation.org/doi/10.1063/1.1753847 |journal=Applied Physics Letters |volume=3 |issue=11 |pages=199–201 |doi=10.1063/1.1753847 |bibcode=1963ApPhL...3..199G |issn=0003-6951|url-access=subscription }}</ref> established scaling laws for gas-discharge lasers,<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=White |first1=A. D. |last2=Gordon |first2=E. I. |date=1963-12-01 |title=EXCITATION MECHANISMS AND CURRENT DEPENDENCE OF POPULATION INVERSION IN He–Ne LASERS |url=https://aip.scitation.org/doi/10.1063/1.1753846 |journal=Applied Physics Letters |volume=3 |issue=11 |pages=197–199 |doi=10.1063/1.1753846 |bibcode=1963ApPhL...3..197W |issn=0003-6951|url-access=subscription }}</ref> and developed frequency stabilization methods for such devices.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=White |first=A. |date=November 1965 |title=Frequency stabilization of gas lasers |journal=IEEE Journal of Quantum Electronics |volume=1 |issue=8 |pages=349–357 |doi=10.1109/JQE.1965.1072246 |bibcode=1965IJQE....1..349W |issn=1558-1713}}</ref> The first continuous-wave visible laser, invented by White and Rigden, is still widely used in research and education, and is a part of various instruments.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Lindley |first=David |date=2010-12-10 |title=Landmarks: The First Laser to Stay On |url=https://physics.aps.org/story/v26/st24 |journal=Physics |language=en |volume=26}}</ref>

White also made significant contributions to the development of lenses for microlithography, as well as methods for aligning a lithographic mask using special lenses and [[Fresnel zone plate]]s.<ref>{{Cite journal |doi=10.1364/AO.13.002693 |title=Digital Wavefront Measuring Interferometer for Testing Optical Surfaces and Lenses |year=1974 |last1=Bruning |first1=J. H. |last2=Herriott |first2=D. R. |last3=Gallagher |first3=J. E. |last4=Rosenfeld |first4=D. P. |last5=White |first5=A. D. |last6=Brangaccio |first6=D. J. |journal=Applied Optics |volume=13 |issue=11 |pages=2693–3303 |pmid=20134757 |bibcode=1974ApOpt..13.2693B }}</ref>
